doc.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Freddie Green and the Basie rhythm guitar
summary: Johnson recounts befriending Freddie Green, urging him to document his style, and describes Green as the pulse of the Basie band.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I want to ask you a question now about working with Basie. From the standpoint of a guitar player, I want you to tell us how that almost now patented Freddie Green kind of guitar playing helped that incredible Basie rhythm section.

Now see, when I got a chance to work with Basie, Freddie was still around, but Basie wasn’t playing anymore, because he was kind of sick. But by working with the band all the other guys were still there. And Freddie Green came through, I was working in Chicago with Joe. And he came after their show and sat down and listened to us. And he came up to me. I knew who he was, but I didn’t think he knew who I was. And he came up to me and he really enjoyed my guitar playing. So we became friends. And I always asked him, “Freddie, you know the type of guitar that you’re playing is not documented, you know you’ve got to do something with the style to leave it on to the rest of the folks.” And he said, “Okay, okay, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.” And he never got around to doing it. And right before he left us he was talking about doing it, because I told him different ways to do it now, and he doesn’t have to write down anything, he can just do it right into © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

a computer, and you know it’ll go right up on the screen. And so when I finally convinced him to do that then he left us. But the style that, when I first saw the Basie band, Freddie’s style was more felt than heard, you know? And when you listened for it you could hear it. Because it was like the pulse of the band. It was pumping the band all of the time. And at any time that you could decipher each instrument, you know what each instrument was doing, you could always hear Freddie Green. And when you hear all the other instruments you could always feel them. He was like the pulse of the whole band, right along with the drummer. And that style of playing is no longer, not the way that he did it, it’s no longer with us. Now the guy that plays with the Basie band now, I think his name is T.J., he is very good at what he does too. But there is only one Freddie Green. And so I will always remember him as you know, joking with him and getting him to admit that he needs to do this, and he never did, but still he was a great human being. He was always very complimentary and always uplifting.
